name: Saururaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Saururus cernuus as a rhizomatous wetland magnoliid with alternate leaves and petiole-adnate stipules, but no floral perianth: tiny exposed flowers are packed into a long spike-like raceme and mature into a schizocarp.

project_scope.note: Saururus cernuus is accepted by current Kew and its native range includes Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with habitat and the inflorescence. Saururaceae project plants are aromatic rhizomatous wetland herbs. Saururus carries a long spike-like raceme of many tiny naked flowers—there are no sepals or petals.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Perennial rhizomatous wetland herb. Leaves alternate, simple and entire. Stipules are present and adnate to the petiole, forming a sheath.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual and perianthless, each subtended by a small bract. In Saururus, stamens are usually 6–8 and carpels are distinct or joined only at the base; ovary is superior.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Schizocarp breaking into usually 3–4 indehiscent one-seeded mericarps.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Wet rhizomatous herb + stipular petiole sheath + long lizard-tail raceme of tiny flowers with no petals/sepals = Saururus/Saururaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: wetland habit → petiole/stipule sheath → drooping raceme → naked flower macro → separate carpels/styles → schizocarp → Piperaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Saururus looks floral from a distance only because hundreds of tiny naked flowers are packed together. Under magnification, each flower has stamens and carpels but no showy perianth at all.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the lizard-tail raceme
steps.look_for: A long narrow white spike-like raceme, often arching or drooping toward the tip.
steps.why_it_matters: This gives the plant its common name and the fastest whole-plant cue.

steps.title: 2 · Find the stipule sheath
steps.look_for: Membranous stipule tissue adnate to the petiole and wrapping the stem/node region.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a strong vegetative family clue and contrasts with exstipulate Lauraceae.

steps.title: 3 · Prove the flowers are naked
steps.look_for: Stamens and pistils exposed directly around the axis with no sepals or petals.
steps.why_it_matters: Perianth absence is one of the most memorable Saururaceae characters.

steps.title: 4 · Count the reproductive parts
steps.look_for: Usually 6–8 stamens and 3–4 carpels/styles, with the carpels free or united only near the base.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms Saururus architecture beyond the raceme silhouette.

steps.title: 5 · Follow the flower into a schizocarp
steps.look_for: Fruit splitting structurally into several indehiscent one-seeded mericarps rather than forming a fleshy fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates this wetland magnoliid sharply from Lauraceae and Magnoliaceae fruit plans.

steps.title: 6 · Compare with Piperaceae
steps.look_for: Both families can have tiny perianthless flowers in spikes; Saururus adds petiolate leaves with stipules and the characteristic long lax raceme/schizocarp architecture.
steps.why_it_matters: Keeps the closest Piperales confuser in the lesson.

comparisons.title: Saururaceae vs Lauraceae
comparisons.rule: Saururaceae is a rhizomatous wetland herb with stipules and perianthless flowers in a raceme; Lauraceae is woody, exstipulate, and has tiny but definite 3-merous tepals plus a one-seeded fleshy fruit.

comparisons.title: Saururaceae vs Magnoliaceae
comparisons.rule: Saururaceae reduces each flower to exposed stamens/carpels with no perianth, while Magnoliaceae has exceptionally large flowers with numerous tepals, stamens and pistils.

comparisons.title: Saururaceae vs Piperaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Piperales and can have tiny perianthless spicate flowers. Project Saururus has distinct petiolate leaves with stipules and a long loose spike-like raceme, then schizocarpic fruit.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not confuse the whole raceme with a single flower. The white 'tail' is an inflorescence made of many tiny individual perianthless flowers.

genera.fast_cue: rhizomatous wetland herb + petiolate stipulate leaves + long perianthless flower raceme + schizocarp

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range extends from eastern Canada through the eastern U.S. into Texas and Mexico.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label stamens, carpels, bract and explicitly show no sepals/petals
label inflorescence axis versus individual flowers
